checks.gcc_parity: Our clang on the same 14 probe cases x O0/O1/O2/Os (gcc/clang.txt) agrees with GCC on 54 of 56. Both differences are clang accepting more: static const at O0, because clang CodeGen folds a const-var load, and a noinline static at O1, because of IPSCCP. Both give the correct instruction. Every O0 non-literal is rejected, as in GCC. Out-of-range folded values give a range error.
checks.diagnostics: The back-end error is a proper DiagnosticInfoUnsupported error: clang exits 1 with 'error: argument 3 to '__builtin_pulp_mulsN' must be a constant integer (it is not constant after optimization)', with no crash, no report_fatal_error and no backtrace. Without -g it points at the enclosing function's declaration line (file:line:col, not 'no line' as the result file says). With -g it points at the exact call (loc.c:5:6). Under llc and ld.lld (LTO) it prints 'error: ... in function f' and fails cleanly. -fsyntax-only accepts 'int n=40; mulsN(x,y,n)'. GAP9 GCC -fsyntax-only accepts it too, so this matches GCC and is acceptable.
checks.merging: Default pipeline, O1/O2/O3/Os/Oz: 9 branch shapes in merge/m.c (if/else, ternary, 4-way switch, store-sinking, returns, macsN, clip bounds, loop with an invariant selector, NE16 OUT_CLIP with a run-time selector) all keep separate constant calls and compile under both clang and GCC. The reason is that SimplifyCFG never introduces a PHI for a constant operand of an intrinsic call (replacingOperandWithVariableIsCheap, SimplifyCFG.cpp:2206-2211), so ImmArg is not needed for that. GVN-hoist only merges identical calls. MergeFunctions only merges identical functions. Loop unswitch duplicates and never merges. ConstantHoisting is inert because RISCVTTIImpl::getIntImmCostIntrin returns TCC_Free. InstCombine store sinking merges only the store (checked in IR). The one failing case is GVNSink, which is off by default and enabled only by the hidden '-mllvm -enable-gvn-sink'. It turns 'if(c) W(x,y,3) else W(x,y,4)' into one call with phi(3,4), and GCC-valid code then gets the 'not constant after optimization' error (6 of 9 shapes; merge/s2.ll with opt -passes=gvn-sink). A 'nomerge' call attribute does not stop GVNSink (merge/s3.ll), so no attribute on the .deferred intrinsics would help. Non-blocking, see observations.

non_blocking_observations: GVNSink (hidden, off by default: -mllvm -enable-gvn-sink) merges .deferred calls that have different constant immediates into one call with a phi, which turns GCC-valid code into a false 'not constant after optimization' error. No default -O level is affected, because SimplifyCFG refuses to sink intrinsic calls with differing constant operands. A 'nomerge' attribute does not stop GVNSink. Suggest the note replace 'in principle an IR pass could...' with this concrete statement, and a BACKLOG row if the pipeline ever enables GVNSink.

Acceptance depends on the optimiser in both directions, as with GCC. Examples: 'for (n=0;n<4;n++) r+=mulsN(x,y,n)' at O1/Os is accepted by GCC and rejected by clang (not unrolled). The 16-iteration version at O2 is accepted by clang and rejected by GCC. The SDK does not use such patterns (survey), so this is inherent to the GCC-compatible design, not a defect.

The result file says back-end diagnostics have 'no line' without -g. They actually carry the enclosing function's declaration location, and the exact call location with -g. When a function has several invalid calls that feed one another, only the last one may be reported, because its result becomes UNDEF and the others become dead. Cosmetic.
llc -global-isel aborts with 'unable to legalize' on .deferred. The literal ImmArg PULP intrinsics do the same on int-20 (pre-existing), and clang -fglobal-isel falls back to SelectionDAG and works.
